projects.name: AI.SDLC
projects.outcome: Make planning, traceability, evidence, approval, release, and production proof executable and human-readable.

requirements.text: A human project lead can see plans, requirements, work, verification, evidence, blockers, metrics, and releases in one portal.
acceptance: The portal is generated from the same ledger that CI validates.

requirements.text: Required SDLC controls run automatically instead of relying on a person to remember them.
acceptance: Local hooks and hosted CI fail with nonzero exit codes when applicable proof is missing.

requirements.text: A failed task blocks itself without unrelated legacy debt stopping all other work.
acceptance: Task-scoped validation excludes unrelated transition debt while preserving it in the portal.

requirements.text: The system cannot claim a visible or behavioral outcome from packaging, a new URL, or a changed filename alone.
acceptance: Content revisions require artifact identity and passed before/after outcome evidence.

requirements.text: A human project lead sees current LEQ and JouleWork at task, project, and portfolio levels without manually copying scores.
acceptance: Hooks and CI recompute transparent ledger-derived metrics and reject stale generated state.

requirements.text: Invalid work cannot merge or publish through the authorized path, and successful lifecycle events update the ledger without bypassing review.
acceptance: Protected main requires hosted checks; publication depends on a release gate; release and deployment events propose evidence-bound ledger updates through pull requests.

requirements.text: Validate one strict machine-readable portfolio ledger with numbered requirements and linked work, tests, evidence, approvals, artifacts, and releases.
acceptance: Malformed, incomplete, contradictory, or incorrectly linked ledgers fail validation.

requirements.text: Apply stage-specific change, release, post-deploy, and drift gates with selectable project, task, and release scope.
acceptance: Each lifecycle transition asks only for evidence appropriate to that transition.

requirements.text: Generate a responsive human portal from the authoritative ledger.
acceptance: The portal shows progress, verification, evidence, blockers, next actions, metrics, and release state.

requirements.text: Run the gates from repository hooks and GitHub Actions for change, release, post-deploy, and scheduled drift transitions.
acceptance: Actual hosted workflow runs are distinguished from merely committing workflow files.

requirements.text: Bind content-change claims to immutable artifact hashes and passed visual, motion, or behavioral comparison evidence.
acceptance: A delivery-only artifact fails any release that claims changed content.

requirements.text: Compute and publish deterministic traceability-v1 metrics from work, tests, evidence, blockers, and completion state at every ledger level.
acceptance: Task metrics roll up to project and portfolio metrics; absent recorded work or a measured source stays unknown.

requirements.text: Bind release and deployment automation to real lifecycle events and open reviewable ledger-update pull requests after the relevant gate passes.
acceptance: The authorized publish workflow cannot run before the release gate; production proof is never invented from deployment status alone.

requirements.text: Protect main with pull-request and required hosted-check rules.
acceptance: GitHub API evidence shows direct invalid merges and force/deletion operations are blocked.

evidence.summary: The repository contract, built-in self-test, 24 lifecycle-hook tests, and 14 portfolio/automation tests passed with zero failures, including positive and intentional negative transition cases.
The implemented validator passes complete linked work and rejects malformed, contradictory, stale, unapproved, unproven, or incorrectly packaged states.
The public and private portals rendered at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths with zero browser console errors; private portfolio data remains outside the public repository.
The operator explicitly authorized implementation, verification, and public GitHub promotion of the AI.SDLC upgrade.
The v0.2.0 npm tarball identity was calculated from its actual bytes.
Hosted GitHub Actions passed the executable change gate and the Ubuntu/Windows Node.js 20/24 validation matrix for commit 56831973820d5eb63846a1234b3bd38e4e87dbda.
The repository contract, built-in self-test, 24 lifecycle-hook tests, and 17 portfolio/automation tests passed; protected regression and YAML lint also passed.
The live local portal rendered its task/project/portfolio metrics at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths with zero console errors or warnings.

The live GitHub API confirms protected main requires pull requests, five hosted checks, current-base strictness, conversation resolution, and admin enforcement; force pushes and deletion are disabled.
The v0.2.1 npm tarball identity was calculated from its actual bytes.
Regression cases prove ledger-derived metric rollups, deterministic board sync, lifecycle-event recording, rejection without production proof, and publish-job dependency on the release gate.
The operator required the final completion audit, correction of public release quality, closure of authorized automation gaps, and public promotion only after proof.
